title: Dynamics 365 Sales Review (2026)
intro: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales is the Dynamics CRM sales application for pipeline management, forecasting, Microsoft 365 interoperation, and Copilot/agent workflows. This review covers verified Sales plan pricing, core CRM capabilities, Copilot positioning, limitations, and who should buy — based on official first-party Microsoft sources.
summary: Dynamics 365 Sales is a strong enterprise CRM for Microsoft shops and a weak fit for simple SMB pipeline buyers. Scores reflect live first-party pricing/product research — not hands-on product testing.
verdict: Dynamics 365 Sales is a strong enterprise CRM for Microsoft 365 organizations that need deep sales force automation, Copilot assistance, and Power Platform extensibility. It is a weak fit for simple SMB pipeline CRM buyers seeking lightweight tools. This review is based on first-party Microsoft product, pricing, and Learn documentation — not hands-on product testing.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Dynamics 365 Sales is a full Microsoft enterprise CRM on Dataverse/Power Apps. Documented capabilities are rich, but the learning/admin surface is far heavier than SMB pipeline CRMs — score reflects Microsoft-shop usability, not lightweight onboarding.
First-party pages emphasize opportunity/pipeline workflows, Copilot pipeline catch-up, scoring/prioritized work lists, and forecasting — strong SFA pipeline story for enterprise sales orgs.

Sales engagement/accelerator, Power Automate extensibility, and Premium agentic recommended actions/agents are well documented. Professional is thinner on advanced automation versus Enterprise/Premium.
Microsoft 365/Outlook interoperation and Copilot email drafts/summaries are a core differentiator for Outlook-centric sellers. Not a marketing-automation email suite.
Reporting/dashboards, Power BI analytics, forecasting charts, and Copilot metric queries are first-party strengths for sales managers.
Advanced customization, configurable fields/views, and Power Platform (Power Apps/Automate) extensibility are explicit Enterprise/product strengths.
Native Microsoft 365, Outlook, Teams, Power BI, Power Platform, and optional LinkedIn Sales Navigator bundling make ecosystem integration the standout criterion.
Dataverse/Power Platform enterprise CRM implies meaningful ongoing admin, licensing nuance (Copilot Credits, add-on licenses), and IT involvement — high overhead versus simple SMB CRMs.
Positioned for mid-market/enterprise sales orgs with advanced SFA, governance/security messaging, and agent/platform extensibility as complexity grows.
List prices of $65–$150/user/mo (annual) are steep for simple pipeline CRM buyers. Value improves substantially for organizations already paying for and standardized on Microsoft 365/Power Platform.

faq.question: How much does Dynamics 365 Sales cost?
faq.answer: Microsoft publishes three USD list plans when billed yearly: Sales Professional $65, Sales Enterprise $105, and Sales Premium $150 per user/month. Relationship Sales is variable/contact pricing. Always confirm current regional pricing on Microsoft’s site.

faq.question: Does Dynamics 365 Sales have a free trial?
faq.answer: Yes. Microsoft documents a Dynamics 365 Sales free trial on the pricing page, and Learn documentation links a 30-day trial signup. There is no permanent free Sales CRM plan in the published ladder.

faq.question: How does Dynamics 365 Sales work with Microsoft 365 and Copilot?
faq.answer: Sales Professional is positioned around core SFA with Microsoft 365 interoperation. Enterprise and Premium document Copilot capabilities in Dynamics 365 Sales, Outlook, and Teams (some Teams capabilities may need additional licenses). Premium adds included Copilot Credits for prebuilt/custom sales agents.

faq.question: Which Dynamics 365 Sales plan should most teams buy?
faq.answer: Sales Professional covers core SFA and Microsoft 365 interoperation. Most organizations needing Copilot insights, advanced customization, and forecasting should evaluate Enterprise ($105). Choose Premium ($150) when Sales Insights, AI recommended actions, data enrichment, and included Copilot Credits for agents matter.

faq.question: Is this a hands-on SoftwareGlimpse lab review?
faq.answer: No. This review is approved based on first-party Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales product, pricing, and Learn documentation. SoftwareGlimpse has not recorded hands-on product testing for Dynamics 365 in this assessment.

sections.heading: What Dynamics 365 Sales is
sections.body: Dynamics 365 Sales is Microsoft’s CRM sales app for managing leads and opportunities, collaborating in Microsoft 365, and using Copilot/agents to assist sellers. It runs on Dataverse and is extended with Power Platform — an enterprise platform CRM rather than a lightweight pipeline board.

sections.heading: Pricing and plans
sections.body: Published yearly USD list pricing is Professional $65, Enterprise $105, and Premium $150 per user/month. A free trial is offered. Premium includes 1,000 Copilot Credits per user/month for agents; Relationship Sales bundles LinkedIn Sales Navigator at variable pricing.

sections.heading: Core CRM capabilities
sections.body: Documented strengths include SFA (leads/opportunities/accounts/contacts), Microsoft 365 interoperation, forecasting and dashboards, Power Platform customization, mobile access, Copilot assistance on Enterprise+, and Premium sales agents/enrichment.

sections.heading: Who it’s for
sections.body: Best for Microsoft-centric mid-market and enterprise sales teams. Less ideal for simple SMB buyers who mainly need an affordable visual pipeline CRM without Microsoft platform commitment.

productExperience.summary: Based on Microsoft’s documented Sales workflow, teams capture and qualify leads, advance opportunities with Copilot assistance, collaborate via Outlook/Teams, automate with Power Platform, and manage forecasts/dashboards — with Premium agents extending autonomous qualification and closing assistance.
